intro.speaker: CITY HALL
intro.text: Production just crashed immediately after the v2.1 deployment. The developers swear 'it worked on my machine' and passed Staging. Find out why it broke in Prod.

success.speaker: CITY HALL
success.text: Excellent diagnosis. Staging and Production had different database versions. Bypassing parity checks causes explosions.

failure.speaker: CITY HALL
failure.text: Incorrect diagnosis. Your hasty conclusion led us to rollback the wrong service. Dig deeper into the configuration logs.

targetMisconception: If tests pass, it's safe for production.
rules: Investigate evidence logs across Dev, Staging, and Production
Identify the root cause of the production outage

engineerMode.whatYouDid: You identified an environment drift where Production was running an older database version than Staging, causing the deployment to crash.
engineerMode.realWorld: According to 12-Factor App principles, Dev, Staging, and Prod must remain as identical as possible. If Staging has DB v14 and Prod has DB v12, tests will pass in Staging but migrations or code will fail catastrophically in Prod.
